text:
Maya: heads up — we're seeing a weird bucket of customer requests fail TLS negotiation in prod eu-west-1, only for some subdomains. Symptoms: clients that try HTTP/2 get a default cert from ALB instead of the customer cert, so backend routing goes to the wrong tenant. :eyes:
Raj: is this after the ACM wildcard rotation yesterday?
Maya: possibly, rotation completed at 16:12 UTC. Not all hosts are affected, and it seems to correlate with HTTP/2-enabled clients. HTTP/1.1 works fine.
Sasha: that sounds like an ALPN/ClientHello mismatch: ALB might be choosing a cert before seeing SNI host or vice versa. Do we have tcpdump or ELB access logs?
Maya: I pulled a few pcap snippets from the edge NAT boxes. Here's an openssl test that reproduces it from my laptop:
```
openssl s_client -alpn h2 -servername tenant-alpha.example.com -connect 172.31.45.12:443
```
The server returns cert chain for "*.example.com" when client uses h2, but returns customer-specific SAN when I force http/1.1 (no h2 ALPN).
Raj: interesting. ALB terminates TLS and should choose cert via SNI. Could be two certs with overlapping names in ACM and the wrong chain has higher priority when ALPN h2 is negotiated.
Jules: also check the chain order. Some clients reject if intermediate ordering is off; but that wouldn't change which cert is presented.
Nico: tagging the aws-load-balancer-controller folks — any known ALB bug where ALPN influences cert selection? @OpsBot can you search past incidents for "ALB ALPN cert"?
OpsBot: search results: 2 matches in infra-ops-logs: "alb-alpn-cert-rotation-2025" and "clienthello-alpn-mismatch-egress-probe". Linking threads...
Sasha: can we reproduce from inside the VPC (i.e., via NAT to the ALB public IP) vs external to rule out edge NAT mangling ClientHello?
Maya: yes — did that. Internal->ALB shows correct cert for both h2 and h1. External via NAT sometimes shows wrong cert for h2. So middlebox (egress NAT or our fronting proxies) might be rewriting or truncating ClientHello.
Raj: do we have any TLS interception/proxy on the egress path? We shouldn't, but older iptables mangle rules or L4 LB could be dropping extension bytes, causing ALPN to be unreadable so ALB picks a fallback cert.
Jules: bad path: if ALB can't parse ALPN it might pick a default listener certificate (listener-level cert) before per-rule certs. Check listener cert attachments and rule priorities.
Maya: checking listener config now: attach output:
```
aws elbv2 describe-listeners --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:...:listener/abc
```
Listener has a default cert (arn:aws:acm:...:default) and a set of rule certificates via AWS: not obvious priority mismatch.
Sasha: can you capture ClientHello bytes hitting the ALB (enable ELB access logs + capture raw TLS from pcap)? We need to confirm if SNI is present and whether ALPN extension exists when request arrives at ALB.
Maya: attached a sample hex from pcap where external path -> ALB. Extract shows SNI=tenant-alpha.example.com present but ALPN extension missing in that capture.
Nico: aha. So the ClientHello arriving to ALB lacks ALPN, client originally sent it, but something in the egress path removed/truncated ALPN extension. That explains difference between internal vs external.
Raj: which component sits between client and ALB on external path? NAT gateway -> edge proxies -> public ALB? We have edge reverse proxies for WAF/CDN. Could be our TCP proxy (go-proxy) not handling TLS extension parsing properly when proxying in passthrough mode.
Jules: action items: 1) Identify the proxy version on the failing egress path and roll back to a build known-good. 2) Add a temporary rule on ALB to prefer customer certs at listener level (if possible). 3) Add metric/alert for ALPN presence in ClientHello from pcap sampling.
Sasha: mitigation: if incoming ClientHello lacks ALPN but has SNI, ALB should still be able to pick cert by SNI. But earlier note about default cert suggests our listener rules might match before rule-based certs when ALPN/HTTP2 behavior is detected. AWS docs note behaviour differences for HTTP/2 listeners.
Maya: for immediate mitigation we can: a) enable a dedicated ALB listener (443) with explicit certificate chain for the affected host and higher priority rule; b) add health-route fallback in ingress so that tenant gets routed even if cert fallback occurs. Both are operationally heavy.
Nico: we can also force clients to use HTTP/1.1 as temporary workaround (via SDK config) for impacted customers. Not ideal.
Raj: let's get telemetry: Sasha please script an automated curl probe from multiple egress points with `curl --http2 -v --resolve tenant-alpha.example.com:443:LB_IP https://tenant-alpha.example.com/` and log whether cert is expected. Run from external egress pools and internal.
Sasha: started a short run, sending results to #eng-infra-monitoring.
Maya: I'm going to isolate the edge proxy version for failing path and spin up a canary with TLS passthrough disabled so it terminates TLS properly (to preserve ClientHello). Will post updates.
Jules: also open a support case with AWS if we confirm ALB is choosing default cert in presence of SNI but missing ALPN — we might be hitting a corner-case bug.
Nico: +1 on support case. Also add a note for Dedicated customers: if they route through our public edge, they could get impacted — consider recommending private ingress or dedicated ALB.
Maya: thanks team. I'll update here after the canary deploy. :thumbsup:
Raj: ping me if you want to revert proxy rollout.
Sasha: probe results: 7/20 external egress nodes show ALPN stripped. internal probes all good. Correlates with edge proxy version v1.14.2.
Maya: confirmed — canary switching those proxies to v1.14.1 fixed ALPN retention. Rolling back v1.14.2 on the affected pool now.
Nico: nice work. Follow ups: add unit/integration tests to proxy CI to assert passthrough doesn't drop TLS extensions, and schedule a postmortem to cover rollout gating.
Maya: creating incident ticket and postmortem stub. Will link here when ready.
